questions.q: How many persons does the French imperative have?
choices: Four: tu, il, nous and vous
questions.why: The imperative exists only for tu, nous and vous, and the subject pronoun itself disappears: Finis ! Finissons ! Finissez !

questions.q: Give the tu imperative of « manger ».
questions.why: -er verbs drop the final -s of the tu form in the imperative: tu manges → Mange ! Verbs in -ir and -re keep it (Finis ! Attends !).

questions.q: Type what you hear. It is a command addressed to tu.
questions.why: An -er verb loses its -s in the tu imperative, and the object pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen, me becoming moi.

questions.q: Why is it « Vas-y ! » with an s, when the imperative of aller is « Va ! » ?
choices: Because y is a plural pronoun
For pronunciation: the s comes back before y and en so the liaison works
Because aller is irregular in every form
questions.why: The -s reappears purely so there is a consonant to link onto: Vas-y ! Manges-en ! Without it the phrase would stumble.

questions.q: Which four verbs build their imperative from the subjunctive?
questions.why: avoir (aie, ayons, ayez), être (sois, soyons, soyez), savoir (sache, sachons, sachez) and vouloir (veuille, veuillons, veuillez) are the irregulars.

questions.q: Formal request: ___ vous asseoir. (the politest way to say « please sit down »)
questions.why: Veuillez + infinitive is the standard formal formula: Veuillez patienter, Veuillez agréer mes salutations. Veux and voulez are almost never used as commands.

questions.q: Build the positive command: Give it to me.
questions.why: In a positive command the pronouns follow the verb, joined by hyphens, direct before indirect, and me becomes moi: « Donne-le-moi. »

questions.q: Build the negative command: Don't give me the book.
questions.why: A negative command puts the pronoun back before the verb in its normal place, and me stays me: « Ne me donne pas le livre. »

questions.q: Which tu imperative is correctly spelled?
questions.why: Only -er verbs (plus aller, ouvrir, offrir, souffrir) drop the -s. An -re verb keeps the present tu form intact: tu attends → Attends !
The reflexive pronoun moves back in front of the verb and reverts to te, which elides before the vowel of inquiète.

choices: en + the nous form of the present minus -ons, plus -ant
à + the je form of the present, plus -ant
questions.why: nous parlons → en parlant, nous finissons → en finissant, nous buvons → en buvant. The nous stem is what keeps the irregular verbs regular here.
Nous faisons gives the stem fais-, so the gérondif is en faisant. The only three genuine irregulars are en ayant, en étant and en sachant.

questions.q: Join with a gérondif: « Il apprend le français et il lit des livres. » → Il apprend le français ___ des livres.
questions.why: Nous lisons → en lisant. Here the gérondif answers « how? » — he learns by reading, the same subject doing both actions.

questions.q: When can you not use a gérondif, and what do you use instead? Give an example of each.
a: The gérondif's action must belong to the sentence's subject. One subject: Elles cuisinent en écoutant de la musique. Two subjects: you need pendant que — Je cuisine pendant qu'elle écoute de la musique.
questions.why: One subject, always. This is the single constraint on the gérondif, and pendant que is the escape hatch when the two actions belong to different people.

questions.q: Say this out loud as a command.
questions.why: A positive reflexive command puts the pronoun after the verb with a hyphen, and te becomes toi.

questions.q: Build the sentence: He answered while smiling.
questions.why: En + present participle says two things happen at once, and the subject of both has to be the same person.

questions.q: Build the sentence: She learns French by reading.
questions.why: The gérondif also covers by doing something, not just while doing it. Same form either way.
